result.title: The Geometry of Ignorance: Detecting Suppressed Knowledge in LLMs through Activation Fragmentation
result.summary: Evaluating whether a large language model (LLM) genuinely knows a concept remains a fundamental problem, since behavioral metrics can be fooled by suppression: a model that refuses to answer may still harbor recoverable knowledge. The framework measures the geometric coherence of \textit{anon-vectors}, the differences in hidden states between a concept-specific query and its anonymized paraphrase, and shows that genuine knowledge forms a tight, low-entropy cluster while ignorance forces geometric fragmentation. Across ten instruction-tuned LLMs from three model families, all fragmentation metrics reliably separate known from unknown concepts, and post-unlearning, fragmentation geometry correlates with adversarial recovery across four attack types and five unlearning algorithms, though the direction of that relationship is shown to depend on attack methodology. Furthermore, a layer-resolved analysis reveals that different adversarial mechanisms exploit this geometry at varying depths, with high attack-specific correlations that are invisible to behavioral evaluation. Together, these results constitute a single-phase, attack-free proxy for unlearning robustness that captures aspects of parametric knowledge inaccessible to output-level metrics. A reference implementation is available at https://github.com/AdarPeleg/geometry-of-ignorance

AI.brief_summary: 提出以「anon-vector」（概念查询与其匿名改写之间的隐状态差）的几何一致性来区分 LLM 的真知与被抑制的无知，并在 10 个指令微调模型及多种 unlearning 设置下检验其与对抗性恢复的关系。
AI.relevance_reason: 虽为纯文本且面向 unlearning，但其不依赖输出行为、仅凭隐状态几何碎片化判断内部信息是否可恢复的探针，可能可供核查 LVR 中视觉细节或任务必要信息是否真正保留在 latent 状态里。
